summary: Provisioning timeouts for new hires: duplicate MAC addresses reported from docking station block Autopilot enroll
description:
Issue summary: Multiple new-hire workstations failed Autopilot enrollment during provisioning. Devices repeatedly timed out at the network registration step and did not receive MDM enrollment. Impact: 9 new hires across two cohorts were delayed from completing onboarding (approx. 6–10 minute timeouts per device), increasing manual imaging work by IT ops. Environment: Production Autopilot provisioning in us-west region; affected both docked and undocked laptops attached to the same dock model. Observed on Dell Latitude 7440 and Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Gen5 that use the CalDigit TS4-equivalent A/B dock (vendor-supplied).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect laptop to vendor Thunderbolt dock and PXE/boot into Windows Autopilot OOBE.
2) Proceed with network connectivity and allow Autopilot to reach enrollment endpoint.
3) Observe enrollment hang during device registration/network handshake stage; event viewer shows repeated DHCP/Nic errors.

Logs and evidence:
- DHCP server logs show multiple requests using identical MAC address for different ports/hosts.
- Windows SetupDiag capture shows "Network adapter initialization failed" and retry loop.
- Netsh show interfaces on one affected laptop reported MAC 00:16:3E:XX:XX:XX matching another laptop in the same bay.
- Packet capture attached to linked Confluence doc (see page) with ARP duplication and DHCP ACKs being delivered to wrong host.

Initial mitigation applied:
- IT Ops instructed onboarding team to provision devices undocked on wired network to avoid dock-induced duplication. This allowed enrollment to complete for 7/9 devices.
- For the remaining 2 devices, USB-Ethernet adapters bypassed the dock NIC and succeeded.

Business impact and urgency: Blocking new hire onboarding and causing increased manual imaging time; prioritized P1 due to operational impact and reproducibility.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Initial triage by IT Ops: confirmed timing pattern, observed identical MAC addresses across two devices attached to same dock cluster.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Reproduced locally in lab: attaching two laptops to the same dock resulted in both reporting the same MAC on the host OS after hot-plug sequence.

2026-03-10 13:20 - Hypothesis: Dock firmware is overriding NIC MACs (MAC cloning) to provide persistent identity for docked peripherals; malfunction causes duplicate MACs across multiple docks in same switch segment.
2026-03-10 15:00 - Confirmed DHCP server logs show lease offers granted but ARP resolution conflicts caused retransmits and network stack retries in Windows OOBE.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Vendor engagement: CalDigit-esque vendor support escalated; vendor reproduced issue internally and identified firmware build 1.8.4 as shipping regression that introduced MAC cloning across Thunderbolt ports when using chain-docking firmware.

2026-03-11 12:15 - Workaround validated: disabling dock NIC using dock management utility or using undocked/wired provisioning prevents duplicate MAC behavior and allows Autopilot enrollment to proceed.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Risk assessment: If left unaddressed, bulk provisioning events in open-office labs will be impacted; also causes intermittent network connectivity and inventory inaccuracies in network management system.
2026-03-12 08:10 - Root cause: Faulty dock firmware (1.8.4) that incorrectly applied a static MAC template across multiple dock units when in daisy-chain mode.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Two new-hire cohorts hit this during morning provisioning. I moved most to undocked provisioning but wanted a ticket so we can identify the root cause and stop future churn.
Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Thanks Aisha — collecting DHCP and pcap dumps. Please keep any affected docks isolated for vendor repro. Assigning to Hardware Ops and Network to assist.
Network Team (Emily Rao) 2026-03-10: Confirmed duplicate MACs in DHCP logs. Switch ports show ARP flaps. Tagged as high priority on our end.
Hardware Vendor (CalDigit Support) 2026-03-11: Reproduced and identified firmware regression. Preparing hotfix (v1.8.5) for validation. ETA 48 hours for signed build and release notes.

Liam Chen 2026-03-12: Vendor patch validated in lab and signed build deployed to staging. Imaging workflow updated to avoid docking during initial Autopilot OOBE until fleet update completes. Closing incident with remediation steps below.
Aisha Patel 2026-03-12: Confirmed onboardings for the delayed hires completed after undocked provisioning and later device check-in post-dock firmware update. Thanks team.
resolution: Root cause: Faulty dock firmware (vendor build v1.8.4) that applied identical MAC addresses across multiple docks in daisy-chain mode, causing DHCP and ARP conflicts during Autopilot enrollment.

Fix applied: Vendor released firmware v1.8.5 that removes MAC cloning behavior and corrects port-specific MAC assignment. Firmware pushed to affected dock units in office via Dock Management Utility (DMT).
Workaround applied: For immediate onboarding events, provision devices undocked on wired NIC or use USB-Ethernet adapter until dock firmware is updated.

Config/Process changes: Added a pre-provision checklist step — "disconnect dock during Autopilot OOBE" — to IT onboarding runbook. Updated provisioning playbook in Confluence and created PR to provisioning repo to add a detection flag for duplicate MACs (see related PR).

Follow-ups: (1) Hardware Ops to perform mass firmware rollout to all office docks by 2026-03-18. (2) Inventory to tag affected dock serials and track post-upgrade stability (INT-41260). (3) Network to monitor DHCP/ARP error rate for two weeks post rollout (INT-41302).
